title: Ship the assimilated `watch` skill out of the box at plugin-root skills/
description:
Human directive (2026-07-28): `/watch` must work on ANY computer immediately after installing the hivemind plugin, with zero setup steps inside the project.

Today it does not. TASK-176 delivered `watch` as an addon-pack resource (`packs/watch/descriptor.json`, `scope: project`, `activate_when: always`) whose skill files live at `assimilated-skills/watch/` (owned copy) and `.claude/skills/watch/` (framework dogfood mirror). Neither directory is loaded by a consumer plugin install — Claude Code auto-discovers plugin skills ONLY from plugin-root `skills/`. A consumer therefore sees no `watch` skill at all until someone manually runs `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/pack-ctl.cjs reconcile-apply --repo-root <root>`, which is exactly the manual step the human is rejecting.

Fix: add a third, byte-identical copy at plugin-root `skills/watch/` so the plugin ships it directly and it loads as `/hivemind:watch` on install.

Explicitly IN scope:
- Copy `assimilated-skills/watch/` -> `skills/watch/` byte-for-byte, including `.skillignore` and all of `scripts/`, preserving the "Sources & provenance (hivemind)" block in SKILL.md verbatim (origin/pin/spdx_id/source_integrity/content_integrity/assimilated_at must survive unchanged — the provenance block is the supply-chain record and must not be edited or regenerated).
- Update `tests/plugin-scaffold.spec.js`: `CONSUMER_SHIPPED_SKILLS` is a strict `readdirSync(skills/)` EQUALITY target at line ~252, so `watch` must be added there or the suite fails. Add it via a named const alongside the existing ones, with a comment recording WHY an assimilated third-party skill ships to consumers (human directive: out-of-the-box availability) — this is a deliberate departure from the ui-ux-pro-max precedent, where assimilated skills stay project-scoped and opt-in.
- Add a byte-identity parity sensor asserting `skills/watch/` matches `assimilated-skills/watch/` file-for-file and byte-for-byte (same shape as the existing assimilate parity sensor added for TASK-136), so the shipped copy can never silently drift from the owned/pinned copy.

Explicitly OUT of scope (do NOT do these):
- Do NOT modify any file under `scripts/` in ANY of the three watch copies. They are pinned third-party code covered by `source_integrity`/`content_integrity` hashes in the provenance block; editing them invalidates the pin.
- Do NOT remove `watch` from `packs/watch/descriptor.json` or from `BUILTIN_PACK_DESCRIPTORS` in `src/builtin-packs.js`. The pack path stays intact and additive — removing the resource would make the reconciler compute a REMOVE op against projects that already installed it via the lockfile, deleting a working skill from existing consumer projects.
- Do NOT add `watch` to `FRAMEWORK_ONLY_SKILLS`.

Note on residual runtime deps: the skill still shells out to `python`/`ffmpeg`/`yt-dlp`, which cannot be bundled. Its own `scripts/setup.py` preflight already handles detection and remediation guidance, and SKILL.md already documents the Windows `python` (not `python3`) substitution. This ticket does not attempt to change that.
acceptance_criteria: `skills/watch/SKILL.md` and `skills/watch/scripts/*` exist at plugin root, and the directory is byte-identical to `assimilated-skills/watch/` (verifiable with `diff -r assimilated-skills/watch skills/watch` reporting no differences)

The 'Sources & provenance (hivemind)' block in `skills/watch/SKILL.md` is byte-identical to the one in `assimilated-skills/watch/SKILL.md` — origin, pin, spdx_id, source_integrity, content_integrity and assimilated_at all unchanged

`tests/plugin-scaffold.spec.js` passes: `watch` is added to `CONSUMER_SHIPPED_SKILLS` so the strict `readdirSync(skills/)` equality assertion (line ~252) holds, with a comment recording the human directive and the departure from the opt-in assimilated-skill precedent
A new parity sensor fails loudly if `skills/watch/` ever drifts from `assimilated-skills/watch/` (non-vacuous: prove it fails when a byte is changed, then restore)
`watch` is NOT added to `FRAMEWORK_ONLY_SKILLS`, and the TASK-153 framework-only assertions still pass unchanged

`packs/watch/descriptor.json` and `src/builtin-packs.js` are unmodified — the pack/reconcile path still resolves and applies `watch` exactly as before (existing pack/reconcile/assimilate specs unchanged and green)
No file under `scripts/` in any watch copy is modified (verifiable via `git diff --stat` showing zero changes under `assimilated-skills/watch/scripts/` and `.claude/skills/watch/scripts/`)
`npm run test:all` is green (this ticket touches the plugin delivery surface and a lock spec, so the full gate applies, including `tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js`)

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
Implemented and released, but PARKED AT in_review — no independent reviewer ran (see "Process deviation" below).

## What landed
- `4a5f8be` feat(skills): ship assimilated watch skill at plugin root — `skills/watch/` added as a byte-identical copy of `assimilated-skills/watch/` (10 files incl. `.skillignore` + all `scripts/`), plus `tests/watch-skill-parity.spec.js` and the `CONSUMER_SHIPPED_SKILLS` update in `tests/plugin-scaffold.spec.js`.
- `fb5d385` fix(tests): ignore Python build artifacts in the watch drift sensor — the sensor walks the filesystem rather than git, so running `scripts/setup.py` generated `scripts/__pycache__/` and reddened the gate on a gitignored artifact. Filter added for `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`.
- `dc69180` chore(release): v0.19.0 — plugin.json 0.18.0 -> 0.19.0, CHANGELOG entry, `docs/releases.html` (also backfilled the missing 0.18.0 entry — the site mirror had skipped from 0.17.0), `docs/index.html` VERSION, `tests/publish-config.spec.js` EXPECTED_VERSION.
- Pushed to origin/main and tagged `v0.19.0`.

## AC verification
1. PASS — `diff -r assimilated-skills/watch skills/watch` reports no differences; 10 files present.
2. PASS — provenance block byte-identical; origin/pin/spdx_id/source_integrity/content_integrity/assimilated_at unchanged (asserted in the new spec).
3. PASS — `watch` added to `CONSUMER_SHIPPED_SKILLS` with a comment recording the human directive and the departure from the ui-ux-pro-max opt-in precedent; the strict `readdirSync(skills/)` equality assertion holds.
4. PASS — sensor proven NON-VACUOUS: appending a byte to `skills/watch/scripts/download.py` produced "skills/watch/scripts/download.py differs from the pinned assimilated-skills/watch/scripts/download.py"; file restored and re-verified identical. It then independently caught the real `__pycache__` drift above.
5. PASS — `watch` not in `FRAMEWORK_ONLY_SKILLS`; TASK-153 assertions unchanged and green.
6. PASS — `git diff --stat` shows zero changes to `packs/` and `src/builtin-packs.js`; pack resource assertion added to the new spec.
7. PASS — zero changes under `assimilated-skills/watch/scripts/` and `.claude/skills/watch/scripts/`.
8. PASS — `npm run test:all`: 1919 passed / 4 skipped, 166 files. `claude plugin validate`: passed. No dist rebuild needed (no `src/` or `bin/` change); dist-parity green.

## Runtime verification (beyond the ACs)
Ran the shipped copy's preflight on Windows. Before binaries: `status: needs_install_and_key`, `missing_binaries: [ffmpeg, ffprobe, yt-dlp]`, and it printed the correct winget commands. After `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` + `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp` (human-approved): `missing_binaries: []`, `status: needs_key` (Whisper key is encouraged, not required). The shipped copy executes.

## Process deviation — READ BEFORE CLOSING
CLAUDE.md Workflow step 6 requires a fresh-context `reviewer` subagent spawn before a green close. That did NOT happen: this session runs under an operator guardrail forbidding subagent spawns unless the human asks for one. The verification above is the Orchestrator's own, not an independent gate, and it is self-reported by the same context that wrote the code — which is exactly the conflict the reviewer role exists to remove.

Left at `in_review` deliberately rather than closed. To finish properly, either spawn the `reviewer` on the range `c3e7067..dc69180` (review_depth: full — new consumer-facing delivery surface, a lock-spec change, and a release), or accept it as-is and close manually.

Note: the release was pushed BEFORE review, at explicit human direction, so a review finding would require a follow-up release rather than an amend.
